title: The Museum of Unsent Letters
synopsis: A museum that opens for one hour each year offers to deliver a letter you never sent—but every delivery changes two lives.

nodes.text: The invitation arrives in your own handwriting, though you have never seen the black envelope before. It names a museum absent from every map and promises one service: bring the letter you most regret not sending. At 2:07 a.m., a brass door appears between the laundromat and the closed florist downstairs.

choices.text: Bring the letter you wrote to your mother
choices.consequence: You bring the letter you wrote to your mother. The decision moves you toward The Archivist and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Enter empty-handed and ask who invited you
choices.consequence: You choose to enter empty-handed and ask who invited you. It opens the route to Shelves Without End, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: An archivist with ink-stained cuffs weighs your letter on a silver scale. The needle trembles between APOLOGY and EXPLANATION. “We can deliver it to the day it was meant for,” she says, “or to the person your mother became after never receiving it.

choices.text: Send it backward to the day you left home
choices.consequence: You send it backward to the day you left home. The decision moves you toward The Kitchen, Twelve Years Ago and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Send it to your mother as she is now
choices.consequence: You choose to send it to your mother as she is now. It opens the route to The Address She Never Gave You, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Beyond the desk, millions of sealed letters rise in dark wooden stacks. Some hum with anger; others are almost weightless. The archivist admits your invitation was written by a future visitor using your name. Before she can explain, one envelope falls open at your feet. It is addressed to you from your mother.

choices.text: Read your mother's unsent letter
choices.consequence: You commit to read your mother's unsent letter. By Dear You, Whenever You Are Ready, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Leave it sealed and search for the future visitor
choices.consequence: You commit to leave it sealed and search for the future visitor. By Portrait of a Visitor, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: The delivery room becomes your childhood kitchen. Your younger self stands in the hall with a packed bag while your mother pretends to wash an already clean cup. The letter can change what happens next, but the archivist warns that you will keep only one version of this memory: the repaired one or the true one.

choices.text: Place the letter where your mother will find it
choices.consequence: You commit to place the letter where your mother will find it. By A Memory Rearranged, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Give it to your younger self instead
choices.consequence: You commit to give it to your younger self instead. By What You Needed Then, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: The museum prints a current address beneath your mother’s name. It is three streets from your apartment. She has been living nearby for four years, respecting the silence she believed you requested. A courier waits beside a bicycle made of folded envelopes and asks whether the letter should arrive alone or with you behind it.
nodes.sceneTitle: The Address She Never Gave You

choices.text: Let the courier deliver it first
choices.consequence: You let the courier deliver it first. The decision moves you toward Across the Street and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Carry it to her door yourself
choices.consequence: You choose to carry it to her door yourself. It opens the route to Three Knocks, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: Your mother’s letter contains no defense. She writes that love can be sincere and still fail someone, that she mistook providing answers for listening, and that she would accept any boundary except one built from a lie you both kept repeating. At the bottom she asks a single question: What happened from your side?
nodes.sceneTitle: Dear You, Whenever You Are Ready

choices.text: Answer her question in a new letter
choices.consequence: You choose to answer her question in a new letter. It opens the route to A Page That Does Not Judge, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Take her letter home without answering
choices.consequence: You take her letter home without answering. The decision moves you toward The Letter You Keep and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: In the final gallery, portraits show everyone who has ever used the museum. Your future self hangs in the last frame, older and calmer, holding two unopened letters. A plaque says you founded this place after learning that closure is not the same thing as an answer. The painted eyes turn toward a small writing room.

choices.text: Meet the future version of yourself
choices.consequence: You commit to meet the future version of yourself. By The Founder, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Refuse the prophecy and enter the writing room
choices.consequence: You refuse the prophecy and enter the writing room. The decision moves you toward A Page That Does Not Judge and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Your mother finds the letter before you leave. The argument becomes a conversation—not gentle, not perfect, but honest enough to alter the years ahead. New memories flicker into place: cautious phone calls, a graduation seat filled, ordinary Tuesdays shared. One old truth begins disappearing with them: the person you became while surviving alone.

choices.text: Accept the kinder history
choices.consequence: You choose to accept the kinder history. It opens the route to The Kinder History, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Restore the life you actually lived
choices.consequence: You restore the life you actually lived. The decision moves you toward Nothing Erased and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Your younger self reads the first line and knows exactly who you are. They do not ask whether life improves. They ask whether leaving was cruel. You can offer the comfort you spent years waiting to hear, or tell them the harder truth: protecting yourself may hurt someone and still be necessary.

choices.text: Tell them they are not cruel
choices.consequence: You choose to tell them they are not cruel. It opens the route to Nothing Erased, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Tell them courage can still carry guilt
choices.consequence: You choose to tell them courage can still carry guilt. It opens the route to Tea Before Answers, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

nodes.text: You watch from a museum bench that now faces your mother’s building. The courier leaves the envelope. A lamp comes on upstairs; a silhouette reads without moving. Ten minutes later the front door opens. Your mother steps outside with no coat, looking both directions as if she has remembered how hope works but not where to find it.

choices.text: Cross the street
choices.consequence: You choose to cross the street. It opens the route to Tea Before Answers, giving up the protection of pretending you had not decided.

choices.text: Let the letter be enough for tonight
choices.consequence: You let the letter be enough for tonight. The decision moves you toward The Letter You Keep and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Your mother opens the door before the third knock. For a long moment neither of you performs surprise. You hold out the letter; she asks whether you want tea. The museum clock sounds in the distance, warning that its hour is almost over and any conversation begun inside its magic must be chosen freely to continue.

choices.text: Go in for tea and begin without the letter
choices.consequence: You go in for tea and begin without the letter. The decision moves you toward Tea Before Answers and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Give her the letter and ask for time
choices.consequence: You give her the letter and ask for time. The decision moves you toward The Letter You Keep and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: The writing room offers paper but no eraser. You begin with the sentence you avoided for years: I loved you, and I was hurt. The words do not cancel each other. When you finish, the museum offers two envelopes—one addressed to your mother, the other to the person you were when silence felt safest.
nodes.sceneTitle: A Page That Does Not Judge

choices.text: Send the letter to your mother
choices.consequence: You send the letter to your mother. The decision moves you toward Tea Before Answers and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

choices.text: Send it to your younger self
choices.consequence: You send it to your younger self. The decision moves you toward Nothing Erased and tells everyone present what you are willing to risk.

nodes.text: Your future self steps out of the portrait and sets two letters on the table. One contains reconciliation; the other, a peaceful goodbye. “I cannot tell you which I chose,” they say. “The museum exists because both can be acts of love.” They offer you the keys, but taking them means remaining after the brass door vanishes.

choices.text: Take the keys and keep the museum open
choices.consequence: You commit to take the keys and keep the museum open. By Keeper of the Unsaid, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

choices.text: Leave both futures unwritten and go home
choices.consequence: You commit to leave both futures unwritten and go home. By Nothing Erased, the choice has already shifted who trusts you and who begins to watch.

nodes.text: You wake with photographs from years you never lived and a dozen affectionate messages waiting on your phone. The loneliness is gone. So are several fierce, beloved parts of the life it pushed you to build. You grieve them quietly, then call your mother. A kinder history is still a history; now you must learn how to inhabit it.

You keep the life that happened—the hurt, the distance, and the strength that grew around both. Yet the memory no longer feels like a locked room. When the museum disappears, the florist’s window reflects someone capable of honoring the past without living inside it. In your pocket is a blank page for whatever comes next.

You do not solve twelve years in one night. You make tea. You say what can be said, stop when it becomes too much, and agree on a day to try again. At 3:00 a.m. the museum vanishes, but the ordinary door across from you remains open. For now, ordinary is more than enough.

Not every unsent letter is unfinished business. Sometimes it is a record of what you survived and what you are not ready to reopen. You leave the museum with both letters in your coat. Months later, you read them without shaking. Whether you ever send one matters less than knowing the choice is finally yours.

The brass keys warm in your hand. Shelves unfold beyond the walls, full of apologies, confessions, boundaries, and goodbyes waiting for honest timing. When the next visitor arrives, you do not promise delivery will fix anything. You promise only a quiet room, a truthful page, and the dignity of choosing what happens to it.
